title: AI & LLM Essentials
blurb: The words that change what you get out of a model — how it reads you, what it knows, and where it fails.

entries.gloss: The chunk of text a model actually reads — words are split into these pieces.
entries.context: In pricing talk you are billed per token; in limits talk the same word is the size of what the model can hold at once.
entries.usage: Estimate how many tokens my document will use, and what fits in the remaining context.

entries.gloss: Everything you hand the model to shape its response — instructions, examples, and data.
entries.context: In casual use it is the question you typed; in engineering it is a versioned artifact with roles, guards, and test cases.
entries.usage: Rewrite my prompt so the model answers with a table and cites its sources.

entries.gloss: Tying the model's answer to specific supplied sources instead of its memory.
entries.context: In retrieval systems it means citing fetched documents; in vision models it means pointing at regions of the image.
entries.usage: Answer strictly from the grounded context below; if the sources don't cover it, say so.

entries.gloss: When a model produces fluent, confident text that is simply not true.
entries.context: In benchmarks it is measured against a fixed answer key; in production it is mostly managed by grounding and review, never eliminated.
entries.usage: Check my draft against the sources and flag any sentence that hallucinates a fact.

entries.gloss: A list of numbers representing meaning, so similar things sit close together.
entries.context: In search talk embeddings power similarity matching; in personalization talk they are the profile built from your behavior.
entries.usage: Explain why two sentences with different words can still have similar embeddings.

entries.gloss: Extra training on your own examples to change how a model behaves by default.
entries.context: In style talk it teaches tone and format; in knowledge talk it is the wrong tool — facts belong in retrieval, not weights.
entries.usage: Decide whether my use case needs finetuning or just better retrieval, and say why.

entries.gloss: A dial for randomness — low keeps answers steady, high makes them varied.
entries.context: In extraction pipelines it is pinned near zero; in creative drafting it is raised, trading reliability for surprise.
entries.usage: Set an appropriate temperature for extracting invoice fields, and explain the choice.

entries.gloss: The moment a trained model actually runs and produces an output for you.
entries.context: In cost talk it is the per-request bill; in latency talk it is the seconds you wait, often split across many servers.
entries.usage: Compare running inference locally versus via an API for a privacy-sensitive app.

entries.gloss: A model that handles more than text — images, audio, or video in and out.
entries.context: In demos it means uploading a photo to ask about it; in accessibility talk it is the difference between an app and a service.
entries.usage: Describe a multimodal flow that reads a receipt photo and returns structured expense data.

entries.gloss: How much text the model can consider at once — its working memory (spelled 'context window').
entries.context: In marketing a bigger number means a better model; in practice long contexts cost more and quality can drift before the limit hits.
entries.usage: Given a 100 page PDF, explain whether to stuff the context window or retrieve chunks instead.
